name: ml-validate-vs-additive-fields
description: Reference ml 0.10.7: 'ml validate' flags additive/unknown record fields as schema errors ('must NOT have additional properties') even on its own records, but mutating commands (record/outcome/archive/restore) accept and preserve them. ADR-0023 round-trip gates must assert additive-field survival through mutators, never through validate-clean.

name: cli-parity-envelope-channel-contract
description: ml 0.10.7 channel contract (pinned by probe + differential battery): success envelopes and validate/doctor failure envelopes on STDOUT, status-style handled errors on STDERR; JSON pretty 2-space; no-args prints help to stderr exit 1; unknown command = 2-line stderr hint; warnings never fail doctor exit; doctor --fix exits with PRE-fix result; --quiet suppresses init and the doctor plain report but NOT status or the validate summary; --timing prints Bun-style Done in Nms only for parsed CLIs.

name: oneof-schema-empirical-rule
description: Reference oneOf sub-errors: each branch reports its first MISSING required property; a branch with all required present but type-const mismatch reports its FIRST required property (pseudo-missing). Records with unregistered type fail as `Unknown record \`X\`` instead of the oneOf blob. Join is ";  " (semicolon+2 spaces); validate message = "Schema validation failed:  <joined>" (2 spaces after colon); doctor detail = "domain:line -  <joined>" (no wrapper); plain validate prints the wrapper once then 3-space-indented sub lines. Line addressing is PHYSICAL 1-based (blank lines counted).

name: record-family-parity-contract
description: record: auto-create precedes validation AND dry-run (side effects persist); duplicate = exit 0 advisory (record #N, quiet-gated), --force appends same id new recorded_at; ids = mx-+sha256(type:idKeyField)[:6] independent of store/domain/timestamps; flag-path field order: type, classification, recorded_at, evidence?, tags?, relates_to?, supersedes?, dir_anchors?, outcomes?, payload, files?, id (stdin/batch preserves INPUT order, appends recorded_at/classification/id); evidence auto-fills FULL git HEAD sha in git dirs; edit replaces lists, appends absent keys at line end (relates_to, supersedes, files), never recomputes ids, no-op succeeds; outcome objects: record-time {status,duration,test_results,agent} before payload, ml outcome {status,recorded_at,duration,agent,notes,test_results} after id.

Three json error contracts discovered only in review round 2: (1) edit/outcome unknown-id envelopes print on STDERR not stdout; (2) the json error field strips the plain-mode "Error: " prefix; (3) record missing-flags json text = no prefix + " Example: " single space (plain has "Error: " + newline-2-space "Retry: "). Handled-error json on stderr is NOT universal — per-command probes required.
resolution: Central Failure::handled strips the prefix; per-command envelope_to_stderr set from probe evidence; pinned by differential tests.

description: Sprint 3: our format layer read records leniently (skip malformed lines, tolerate unknown types) while the reference readExpertiseFile THROWS. On a rewrite path (delete/move/delete-domain) that silently erased malformed lines and moved unknown-type records. Lesson: a lenient reader on a WRITE path is a silent-mutation hazard — the reference source is the authoritative spec for such semantics, not probes of clean stores.
resolution: Strict lib reader (records.rs) with typed MalformedLine/UnknownRecordType errors, referenced from the source; rewrites re-serialize compactly with id generation instead of copying raw lines.

name: reference-source-over-probe
description: The shipped reference package source (node_modules/@os-eco/mulch-cli/src) is the authoritative parity spec: probing clean stores missed the lenient/strict reader split, the re-serialization model (JSON.stringify, generated ids, legacy outcome normalization), config default backfill (applyConfigDefaults), domain-order semantics (JS delete vs IndexMap::swap_remove) and resolveRecordId (bare hash, unique prefix, Ambiguous). Read the source BEFORE implementing any command that mutates shared state.

name: store-policies-ownership
description: The .mulch store has ONE owner in the lib (StoreFiles): StoreLocation discovery, config mutations, and the explicit policies — read_records(domain, allow_unknown) (strict: typed MalformedLine/UnknownRecordType before any write; the flag tolerates unregistered types only), read_lines(domain) for reporting commands that must name the offending line, domain_modified(), rewrite_domain (compact canonical re-serialization + id generation + 0-byte for empty), append_domain_line (verbatim, newline guard). The CLI keeps only rendering, messages and channels (commands::open_store owns the no-store policy).
